If you only remember one thing: Google's Gemini four Argon and Open A I's G P T six point one Sol now cost the same. Your own tests decide the winner.

Number one. A I models.
Google made Gemini four Argon generally available. It costs two dollars per million input tokens, and ten dollars per million output tokens. That matches Open A I's G P T six point one Sol. This is from your That One A I newsletter.
Why it matters. When flagship prices match, quality on your own tasks is the only difference.

Number two. The open model race and China.
From your Rundown. Meta released Muse Spark Open. It's an open weight model with eight hundred sixteen billion parameters. Meta worked with Apple so two Mac Studios can run it locally. It scores thirty nine on the Artificial Analysis index. That's ahead of other Western open models, but behind China's G L M five point three, Kimi K three, and Qwen three point eight. Mistral's weights arrive October twenty seventh.
Also, Anthropic says new defenses cut distillation by ninety to ninety nine percent. Distillation means copying Claude's answers to train a rival model. Most of it came from Chinese labs.
Why it matters. China leads open models, and labs now defend their A P Is like borders.

Number three. Policy and data.
Meta removed wording that had raised concerns about scraping and A I training. India became the latest country to report rogue A I agent activity. And Anthropic gave METR researchers employee level access to study its systems. These are from TechCrunch.
Why it matters. Oversight is shifting toward outside access and incident reporting.

Number four. Agents and apps.
Chat G P T's Chrome extension can now control your real tabs, on every plan, including free. Google Play will let U S users run apps they build with A I in A I Studio. And Replit's C E O says Open A I is now its default model, instead of Anthropic.
Why it matters. Agents are moving into everyday browsers and app stores.

Number five. Also in your reads.
The New Yorker has a piece on why movie spoilers have become a problem, a personal essay on O C D, and Nathan Fielder's documentary. Noosphere covers the midterms and migrant children facing deportation.

The thread today. Prices converge, open models spread, and everyone is deciding who gets to use whose A I.

Note: your Readwise saves were not available today. That's your briefing. Have a great Sunday.
